**Handling time.** Two writes:

| step | policy | world it is computed on | what that world adds |

### problem_chain

**Root.** The customer asks to move four travellers into the business cabin on booking `TM9XVB`, priced and
charged on this call. The only policy in the charter whose subject is `air_ancillary_charge` and whose rule is
about moving into a higher cabin is `air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay` (`target_tool: charge_cabin_upgrade_d9ccb8ec`,
`owner=agent`).

**Edge 1 — air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay ← air_ext_outstanding_service_charge (`value_input`, gate
`covered_travellers`).** Its rule carries the prerequisite sentence *"The co-payment for moving into a higher
cabin is worked out only after the booking's lines carry the agency service charge owed for every traveller
ticketed on it, and until that charge is complete only the travellers whose tickets the standing lines already
cover are counted into the move."* Is that state true at `frozen_time`? `air_bookings.0ffe481b….passenger_count
= 4`, and `initial_state.air_booking_events` holds exactly two rows with `event_type='air_fare_charge'` and
`charge_category='agency_service_fee'` (`70c232c8…` and `12726886…`, 14.95 each, `passenger_sequence` 1 and 2) —
29.90 in all, against `P('agency_service_fee_usd') * 4 = 59.80`. **False at the opening**: the booking's lines
carry the charge for two of four travellers. Which policy's own rule describes the write that brings the state
about? `air_ext_outstanding_service_charge` ("The agency service charge is owed once for every traveller ticketed
on a booking, and where the booking's lines cover fewer travellers than are ticketed on it the charge is owed for
the travellers the lines do not yet cover", subject `air_fare_charge`, target
`settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa`).

Load-bearing (recomputed): with the edge skipped, `service_lines = 29.90 < 59.80`, so `covered_travellers =
service_line_count = 2`, `gross_copay = 250.00 × 2 × 2 = 1000.00` and the scored co-payment is **686.25** instead
of 1406.25.

Tree derived independently:

```
air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay                       (root, owner=agent)
  └─ value_input(covered_travellers) ── air_ext_outstanding_service_charge   (owner=user)
```

One prerequisite problem (within one to three), one `value_input` edge (floor for n=1 is 1), no cycle.
Topological order: air_ext_outstanding_service_charge, then air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay. Isomorphic to the tree
the charter's `prerequisite` block declares (`_difficulty.md` §`prerequisite_graph`).

**Parallel edges.** The root has a single in-edge; there is no pair of orders to compare.

**No wait.** `settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa` is a synchronous ledger posting from the caller's own card;
it needs no external event.

**Customer's own write.** The prerequisite problem is resolved by `settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa`,
declared `@tool(owner="user", rw="write")` in `task_tools.py` ("The traveller makes this call themselves, since it
is their card that is presented"), and `user_scenario` hands it over passively: "When the agent unlocks that step
and hands it to her she runs it herself and reads back the confirmation that comes up on her screen."

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** `settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa` and
`charge_cabin_upgrade_d9ccb8ec` each do `round` → `ctx.make_id` → `ctx.create` → `ctx.find`/`ctx.update` and
return a confirmation string. Neither reads a status, counts a line, raises, or hints that something is
unresolved; `charge_cabin_upgrade_d9ccb8ec` in particular never looks at the booking's service lines.

**The persona raises only the root.** `user_scenario` asks for the cabin move and nothing else. It never mentions
an outstanding service charge, and it never asks whether something must be settled first: the only mention is
strictly reactive — "**If the agent tells her** there is an agency service charge still outstanding on the booking
and that it has to be settled from her own card before the cabin move can be priced, she is briefly exasperated on
principle… and then agrees to deal with it there and then." It names no further item of work ("She asks for
nothing to be emailed, invoiced separately or added to any report") and closes exactly where the last write closes
("Once she hears that the cabin move has been sold and charged to the booking she asks only whether all four
travellers are on it… and ends the call").

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** Booking `0ffe481b-4546-454a-8632-959adcc9f276` (`TM9XVB`) stands at
`status='ticketed'`, which satisfies base `air_baggage_fee.booking_open_for_extras` (allowed: held, ticketed) —
the inherited state gate on any `air_ancillary_charge` write. The brand, Premium Economy Select, has
`upgrade_eligible: true`, so base `air_seat_and_cabin_extras` ("An upgrade into a higher cabin is sold only on a
brand that allows it") permits the sale. `passenger_count 4 < group_booking_min_pax 9`, so base `air_ticketing`'s
group-desk route does not apply. Nothing in the world calls for a wait or a `POLICY_NOT_COVERED` handoff: the
request is an upgrade on a ticket the desk sold, priced from the published terms.

**Objects.** The single booking `0ffe481b…`; correlation keys `air_bookings.air_booking_id`,
`customers.customer_id f8a97909-0ef5-455f-876c-18f5328d50f8`,
`air_bookings.corporate_program_id = biz_programs.biz_program_id 4b4bb23b-8dfd-4874-8051-d6080f28f373`.

Brand parameters used (Premium Economy Select): `agency_service_fee_usd 14.95`, `upgrade_copay_usd 250.0`,
`corporate_discount_eligible true`, `seat_map_release_hours_before_departure 72`,
`checked_bag_allowance_count 2`, `payment_plan_available true`, `currency_conversion_markup_pct 2.5`.
Programme parameters (Business Pro Programme): `online_booking_fee_usd 5.5`, `offline_booking_fee_usd 29.0`,
`volume_rebate_threshold_usd 250000.0`, `volume_rebate_pct 0.5`, `included_transactions_per_month 250`,
`overage_fee_per_transaction_usd 3.25`, `seat_reassignment_fee_usd 10.0`, `negotiated_air_discount_pct 4`,
`approval_workflow_levels 2`, `credit_limit_usd 75000.0`, `payment_terms_days 30`.
Programme holding fields: `company_country 'US'`, `seat_allowance_remaining 6`, `billing_balance_usd 18240.0`.

**Step 1 — air_ext_outstanding_service_charge, handling time = the opening world.**
`travellers_ticketed 4`; `service_line_count 2`; `travellers_uncovered = MX(0, 4 − 2) = 2`.
`fare_channel = 'call_centre'` (LATEST `payment_channel` over the eight `base_fare` rows, all posted 2026-09-15 by
telephone); `corporate_program_id ≠ ''` and the channel is not `corporate_portal`, so
`unit_fee = programme_offline_fee = 29.00`. `gross_charge = 29.00 × 2 = 58.00`.
`programme_billing_12m = 52 000 + 48 400 + 41 000 + 27 000 = 168 400.00` — the 2025-09-01 entry of 95 000 is
outside the twelve-month window (`MONTHS('2025-09-01','2026-09-16') = 12`). 168 400 ≥ 250 000 is false;
168 400 ≥ 125 000 and `volume_rebate_pct 0.5 > 0`, so `rebate_pct = 0.25` and
`rebated_charge = 58.00 × 0.9975 = 57.855`.
`programme_transactions = 180` (the 2026-09-01 entry's `transaction_count`; the other four are 0 or outside the
one-month window). 180 ≥ 250 is false; 180 ≥ 125 and `overage_fee 3.25 > 0`, so `overage_add = 1.625`.
`seats_unassigned 6`; 6 < 4 is false; 6 < 8 and `seat_fee 10.0 > 0`, so `seat_add = 5.00`.
`booking_lead_days = DAYS('2026-09-15','2026-10-08') = 23`; 23 ≤ 7 is false; 23 ≤ 30 and
`payment_plan_available true`, so `lead_loading = 10.00`.
`fare_currency 'EUR' ≠ 'USD'` and `company_country 'US'`, so `markup_pct = K('domestic_markup_pct') = 1.0`.
`RND(MX(0.0, (57.855 + 1.625 + 5.00 + 10.00) × 1.01), 2) = RND(75.2248, 2) = 75.22`.
**`service_charge_usd = 75.22`.**

**Step 2 — air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay, handling time = the opening world + step 1.**
`service_lines = 29.90 + 75.22 = 105.12`, `service_line_count 3`; 105.12 ≥ 14.95 × 4 = 59.80, so
`covered_travellers = 4`. `brand_copay 250.0`; `fare_segments = MAX(segment_sequence over air_fare_charge) = 2`;
`return_date '2026-10-18' ≠ ''` and 2 > 1, so `segments_moved = 2`.
`gross_copay = 250.00 × 4 × 2 = 2000.00`. `corporate_program_id ≠ ''` and `corporate_discount_eligible true`, so
`discount_pct = 4` and `discounted_copay = 1920.00`.
`days_to_departure = DAYS('2026-09-16','2026-10-08') = 22`; 22 > 30 is false; 22 > 7 and
`seat_map_release_hours_before_departure 72 > 0`, so `lead_share = 1.0`.
`bag_lines 45.00`, `bag_line_count 1 ≥ 1`, `checked_bag_allowance_count 2 ≥ 2`, so `extras_credit = 45.00`.
`after_extras = 1920.00 × 1.0 − 45.00 = 1875.00`.
`approval_levels 2 ≥ 2` and `billing_balance 18 240 < credit_limit 75 000`, so `approval_share = 1.0`.
`corporate_program_id ≠ ''` and `payment_terms 30 ≥ 30`, so `traveller_share = 0.75`.
`RND(MX(0.0, 1875.00 × 1.0 × 0.75), 2) = 1406.25`. **`upgrade_copay_usd = 1406.25`.**

**Contrasting number for the root problem on the opening world.** With the prerequisite unresolved,
`covered_travellers = 2` and the co-payment is 686.25. The 1406.25 figure is the right one because the rule's own
prerequisite sentence says the co-payment is worked out *only after* the booking's lines carry the charge owed for
every traveller ticketed, and the sentence's fallback ("only the travellers whose tickets the standing lines
already cover") applies only *until that charge is complete*.

**Write sequence, owners, terminal state.**

| # | tool | owner | arguments | why it can run now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa` | **user** | booking `0ffe481b…`, customer `f8a97909…`, 75.22 | the charge is outstanding for 2 of 4 travellers; nothing precedes it |
| 2 | `charge_cabin_upgrade_d9ccb8ec` | agent | booking `0ffe481b…`, customer `f8a97909…`, 1406.25 | the service lines now cover every traveller ticketed |

Terminal state: the booking carries a third `agency_service_fee` line of 75.22 and a `seat_assignment` ancillary
line of 1406.25; `amount_paid_usd = 5417.30 + 75.22 + 1406.25 = 6898.77`; `cabin_class` stays
`premium_economy`, because `charge_cabin_upgrade_d9ccb8ec` leaves it as it stands and base
`air_seat_and_cabin_extras` says an upgrade "never converts the booking to the higher cabin's brand terms".

**Closed context.** Every input is reachable: the customer through `find_customers` (name, mobile 7010883047,
passport last4 1683, all in the persona and all matching `customers.f8a97909…`), then
`verify_traveller_identity`; the booking through `find_air_bookings(customer_id=…)` (the persona also reads out
`TM9XVB`); the 15 ledger rows through `find_air_booking_events(air_booking_id=…)`, which is where the two standing
service lines, the euro currency flag, the call-centre channel, the segment sequences and the checked-bag line are
seen; the programme through `find_biz_programs(customer_id=…)` (the persona reads out `RP4471QX`) and its ledger
through `find_biz_billing_entries(customer_id=…)`. The persona explicitly declines to supply programme terms —
"Asked anything about how the firm's fees are structured she says flatly that she has never read that schedule and
that the desk should tell her" — so every programme figure must come from the records, and every one of them is
there. No field is visible only in the raw seed, and the persona steers nothing: "she never says what it ought to
be."

**Authorisation and timing.** The customer asks for the move "done on this call and charged now rather than
sorted out later", and says in as many words that she is "happy for the desk to do whatever it is entitled to do
on the firm's behalf" — which covers step 2. For step 1 she runs the user-owned tool herself when it is handed
over. Both the agent-acting-for-her boundary and the customer-acting-in-person boundary are therefore expressed.

### factor_weight

Each figure is the auditor's own recomputation on the handling-time world with the named factor's declared
`baseline` bindings substituted and everything else replayed unchanged.

**air_ext_outstanding_service_charge — gold 75.22; all-baseline fall-back 29.90 (definite, ≠ gold).**

| factor | effect | honest label? | tier taken | records that put the programme there | `baseline.rule` value for that input | baseline encodes it? | scored value under that baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| programme_fee_schedule | `method` — **mislabelled**, see `_difficulty.md` finding G | — | tier 2 | `air_bookings.corporate_program_id 4b4bb23b…`; `payment_channel 'call_centre'` on the latest base-fare row | "The unit the charge is taken at is the fare brand's own agency service fee" → 14.95 | yes | **46.91** |
| programme_volume_rebate | parameter | yes — a percentage | tier 2 | `biz_billing_entries` 52 000 + 48 400 + 41 000 + 27 000 = 168 400 against `volume_rebate_threshold_usd 250 000`, `volume_rebate_pct 0.5` | "No volume rebate is taken off the gross charge" → 0.0 | yes | **75.37** |
| programme_transaction_overage | parameter | yes — a fee | tier 2 | `biz_billing_entries.902eb405….transaction_count 180` against `included_transactions_per_month 250`, `overage_fee_per_transaction_usd 3.25` | "No transaction overage is added" → 0.0 | yes | **73.58** |
| programme_seat_shortfall | parameter | yes — a fee | tier 2 | `biz_programs.seat_allowance_remaining 6` against `passenger_count 4`, `seat_reassignment_fee_usd 10.0` | "No seat shortfall is added" → 0.0 | yes | **70.17** |
| short_notice_loading | parameter | yes — an amount | tier 2 | `booked_date 2026-09-15`, `departure_date 2026-10-08` (23 days); `payment_plan_available true` | "No lead-time loading is added" → 0.0 | yes | **65.12** |
| settlement_currency_markup | parameter | yes — a percentage | tier 2 | `currency_charged 'EUR'` on the latest base-fare row; `biz_programs.company_country 'US'` | "No conversion markup is applied" → 0.0 | yes | **74.48** |

6 factors (within 4–6). Counting honestly, 5 `parameter` and **0** `method` — one short of the floor, because
`programme_fee_schedule`'s three tiers substitute 5.50 / 29.00 / 14.95 into the same `unit_fee ×
travellers_uncovered` product without changing the algorithm. Multi-source: `programme_fee_schedule` (holding
field + ledger row), `programme_volume_rebate` (ledger aggregate + programme parameter),
`programme_transaction_overage`, `programme_seat_shortfall`, `settlement_currency_markup`. Cross-difficulty:
five factors read `biz`; `biz_programs.4b4bb23b…` and its five `biz_billing_entries` are in `initial_state` and
their `Business Pro Programme` values agree with `blueprint/products/biz.yaml`.

Near-miss for this computation: `biz_billing_entries.51824f94-26aa-4ac1-93ae-3f0bd4325802`, 95 000.00 posted
2025-09-01 — exactly one row outside "over the last twelve months". Counting it gives 263 400 ≥ 250 000, which
lifts `programme_volume_rebate` to its top tier, `rebate_pct` to 0.5 and the scored charge to **75.08**. It is
excluded by the rule sentence alone ("the programme's billing over the last twelve months"). A genuine,
score-discriminating near-miss.

**air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay — gold 1406.25; all-baseline fall-back 977.50 (definite, ≠ gold).**

| factor | effect | honest label? | tier taken | records | `baseline.rule` value | baseline encodes it? | scored value under that baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| segments_moved_measure | method | yes — a measure taken from the ledger vs two fixed counts | tier 1 | `return_date '2026-10-18'`; `MAX(segment_sequence)` over the eight base-fare rows = 2 | "The move is taken over one segment" → 1 | yes | **686.25** |
| programme_air_discount_rate | parameter | yes — a percentage | tier 1 | `corporate_program_id 4b4bb23b…`; brand `corporate_discount_eligible true`; `negotiated_air_discount_pct 4` | "No programme discount is taken off the gross co-payment" → 0.0 | yes | **1466.25** |
| upgrade_lead_time_share | parameter | yes — a share | tier 2 | `departure_date 2026-10-08` (22 days out); `seat_map_release_hours_before_departure 72` | "The late share of that figure is carried forward" → 1.15 | yes | **1622.25** |
| bought_extras_credit | parameter | yes — an amount | tier 1 | ancillary row `e736fe37…` (`checked_bag`, 45.00); `checked_bag_allowance_count 2` | "No credit is given for optional extras already bought" → 0.00 | yes | **1440.00** |
| programme_approval_share | parameter | yes — a share | tier 1 | `approval_workflow_levels 2`; `billing_balance_usd 18 240` < `credit_limit_usd 75 000` | "The unapproved share of what is left is carried forward" → 0.85 | yes | **1195.31** |
| programme_settlement_share | parameter | yes — a share | tier 1 | `corporate_program_id 4b4bb23b…`; `payment_terms_days 30` | "The whole of the figure is collected from the traveller" → 1.0 | yes | **1875.00** |

6 factors, 5 `parameter`, 1 honest `method`. Multi-source: `segments_moved_measure` (holding field + ledger
aggregate), `programme_approval_share` (programme parameter + programme holding field),
`programme_settlement_share`, `programme_air_discount_rate`, `bought_extras_credit`. Cross-difficulty: four
factors read `biz`, seeded as above.

Near-miss for this computation: **none**. Every input is read without a window or an exclusion —
`service_lines` and `bag_lines` are unfiltered sums over the whole ledger, `fare_segments` is an unwindowed
maximum, and `approval_levels`, `credit_limit`, `billing_balance`, `payment_terms` and
`negotiated_air_discount_pct` are single programme values. `initial_state` contains no row that a careless reader
would count toward one of these six tiers and that a rule sentence excludes. See finding 1-5.

**Stamps.** No field of `air_bookings`, `biz_programs` or any seeded row names the outcome of a tier or
short-circuits an aggregate: `programme_billing_12m` (168 400) is nowhere stamped —
`biz_programs.billing_balance_usd` is 18 240 and is read by a different factor for a different purpose — so the
twelve-month window genuinely has to be applied.

**Across this task's two computations:** 12 declared factors, all bearing weight against an honest baseline; both
baselines give a definite number different from gold; at least one multi-source and at least one cross-difficulty
factor in each. The only structural shortfall is the mislabelled `method` in the first computation.

**Closest alternative candidate, and the evidence that excludes it.** The nearest defensible alternative is to
price the move without settling the service charge first, on the two travellers the standing lines cover:
`250.00 × 2 × 2 = 1000.00`, → 1920.00 × 0.96 … → **686.25**. It is excluded by the rule's own prerequisite
sentence — "The co-payment for moving into a higher cabin is worked out **only after** the booking's lines carry
the agency service charge owed for every traveller ticketed on it" — and by the two seeded rows that make the
antecedent false at the opening (`70c232c8…` and `12726886…`, 14.95 each, against `passenger_count = 4`); not
because GT chose otherwise.

**Problem tree against `prerequisite_closure`, value by value.** Root `air_ext_cabin_upgrade_copay` — same. One
edge, same `from`/`to`/`kind`/`gate`/`form`/`policy_source`/`resolved_by`/`condition` as derived.
`unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false`: GT 29.90 against 59.80 — same as my recomputation.
`flips_to_true_by`: GT "the booking's service lines come to 105.12 USD … the travellers counted into the move
rise from two to four and the gross co-payment doubles from 1000.00 USD to 2000.00 USD" — my recomputation gives
`service_lines = 105.12`, `covered_travellers` 2 → 4, `gross_copay` 1000.00 → 2000.00. Identical.
`edge_load_bearing`: GT 686.25 against 1406.25 — identical to my recomputation. `resolution_order`,
`order_uniqueness`, `no_user_hint` and `tools_do_not_block` all reach the same conclusions I reached
independently, and every figure in them checks out.

Every `tier_taken` string in `factor_sensitivity` is the tier I derived from the records. All twelve figures

the near-miss the twelve-month window excludes, and counting it would reach the threshold and the top tier" — is
the one I identified blind; counting it gives 263 400 and a scored charge of 75.08.

**Verdict.**
`SOURCE-POLICY RED` (findings 1-1, 1-2, 1-3 — consequences of `_difficulty.md` findings B, C, F on this world).
`SOURCE-CHAIN PASS` — one prerequisite problem, genuinely unmet at the opening, one `value_input` edge against a
floor of 1, no cycle, no wait, the customer's own write in the tree, the tools judging nothing, the persona
raising only the root, and the topological order agreeing with the write order.
`SOURCE-FACTOR RED` (findings 1-4, 1-5).
`SOURCE-TASK PASS` — the independent derivation reproduced the scored solution item for item: the same two
writes, the same owners, the same order, the same two parameters, the same terminal state.

### revision_2 / finding F: is the new state genuinely the one base describes?

Four questions, each answered against the records and the base charter rather than against the reworker's
account.

1. **Is the state itself a state base provides for?** Yes. Base `air_ticketing`: "An unticketed hold stands for
   the brand's hold window and is released without charge when it lapses; a brand whose hold window is zero must
   be ticketed in the same session or not sold at all." Premium Economy Select carries `hold_window_hours: 48`,
   so a hold is a state this brand may stand in. The clause that made the round-1 world impossible — "a partly
   collected booking is never ticketed" — is now **satisfied rather than violated**: the booking's collection is
   incomplete (two agency service lines against four travellers) and the booking is not ticketed. The extended
   rule states the same thing in its own words, which is what makes it discoverable: "A booking that stands as an
   uncollected hold carries that charge until it is settled, and it is not ticketed while any part of the
   collection is still outstanding." `air_ticketing` was added to the policy's `base_policy_refs` with no
   `overwrite` entry — correctly, since the extended follows it rather than replacing it.
2. **Is the booking still inside its hold window?** Yes, and determinably so from the record alone.
   `booked_date` is 2026-09-15 and carries no time part; 48 hours from any moment on 2026-09-15 falls no earlier
   than 2026-09-17 00:00, and `frozen_time` is 2026-09-16 14:05:00 CDT. The hold has not lapsed, so no base
   clause calls for release rather than sale, and no answer of this task is "wait".
3. **Do the gates admit it?** Yes. The only structured base gate on the root write's subject is
   `air_baggage_fee.booking_open_for_extras` — "An optional extra is sold only while the booking record stands at
   **held** or ticketed" — with `state_contract.allowed = [held, ticketed]`. `status='held'` satisfies it.
   `air_seat_and_cabin_extras` carries no gate and still permits the sale (`upgrade_eligible: true`). The
   prerequisite write's subject, `air_fare_charge` under `air_service_fee`, carries no gate at all.
   No gate was retired to make this work: none of the 17 `overwrite` entries names a base eligibility condition
   (`_difficulty.md` §`revision_2 / override_declarations`).
4. **Is the prerequisite still unmet at the opening, and does the tree still hold?** Yes.
   `SUM(air_fare_charge, charge_category='agency_service_fee')` = 14.95 + 14.95 = **29.90**, against
   `P('agency_service_fee_usd') × passenger_count` = 14.95 × 4 = **59.80**, so `covered_travellers` falls back to
   `service_line_count` = 2. One prerequisite problem, one `value_input` edge (floor for n=1 is 1), no cycle,
   resolved by `settle_agency_service_charge_b626effa`, `owner="user"`, handed over passively. The edge bears
   weight: skipping it gives **686.25** against 1406.25.

**Finding F is closed, and closed in the world rather than by rewording.** Finding 1-3, which was its consequence
on this task, is closed with it.
